title: Orsen and the Verdict
premise: When a stranger's corpse is found in the cathedral crypt wearing clothes stolen from Orsen Vane's own wardrobe, the town of Marrowfen insists the case was settled years ago — the Verdict, they call it, when a beloved canon was convicted of crimes no one will name. Orsen, whose memory of that night has been quietly failing him, teams up with cathedral archivist Elodie Ravensworth to reopen what everyone swore was closed. Together they discover the crypt's lock was changed three years ago by someone still in power, and that Orsen's missing memories were not lost but taken. In the end, Orsen must testify against the man who edited his mind — discovering the victim wore his clothes to force him to remember — and the true verdict is finally spoken over an open crypt.
about_author: Hazel Yarrow is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing documents no one was meant to read. She writes mysteries about small towns with long memories from a house within earshot of church bells.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: Orsen Vane's POV. Orsen, a watchmaker with gaps in his memory, is summoned to the cathedral where a body lies in the sealed crypt wearing his own gray coat and boots. Elodie Ravensworth, the archivist, notes the crypt's lock was replaced three years ago. The chapter establishes dread and Orsen's quiet terror that he cannot account for his own past.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Secrets
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie shows Orsen the archive: three years of records meticulously filed, yet a whole season of documents missing — the months surrounding the trial the town calls the Verdict. The dead man is identified as a former court clerk who left town after the trial. Elodie feels her careful order cracking; Orsen feels watched.

chapters.title: What the Town Swears By
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen canvasses townsfolk who all repeat identical phrases about the Verdict, as if rehearsed. An old verger hints that Canon Aldous Wren, the convicted man, died in prison innocent. That night someone ransacks Orsen's flat, taking only photographs. The beat is isolation — the whole town closing ranks against one question.

chapters.title: The Missing Season
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie reconstructs the destroyed records from binding scars and ink ghosts, finding that every document naming a certain magistrate, Corven Hale, was excised. She realizes the thefts were done with archival precision — by someone trained like herself. Her pride in her craft curdles into complicity; she may have shelved the cover-up herself.

chapters.title: A Coat That Fits
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A tailor confirms the coat was copied, not stolen — someone commissioned a duplicate of Orsen's wardrobe weeks before the murder. Orsen's memory flickers: a candlelit room, a voice reading aloud, his own voice answering. He begins to suspect his blackouts were engineered. The emotional beat is vertigo — identity itself becoming unreliable evidence.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie finds the trial transcript: Orsen was the star witness against Canon Wren, though he has no memory of testifying. His testimony hinged on details only the killer could know. She confronts him gently; he shatters, convinced he condemned an innocent man. Rising tension peaks as they realize whoever shaped Orsen's memory can unshape it again.

chapters.title: Hypnosis in the Vestry
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A retired doctor reveals Magistrate Hale practiced 'therapeutic suggestion' on witnesses before the Verdict. Under hypnosis, Orsen recovers the night of the crime: he saw Hale, not Wren, leaving the sacristy — and was made to forget. Someone breaks into the vestry mid-session, stealing the recording. Fear turns to resolve.

chapters.title: Dead Man's Errand
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Tracing the murdered clerk's last movements, Elodie discovers he had requested his old files by post — the request answered by a forged letter in her own handwriting. The victim came to warn them both. Elodie realizes she was chosen as archivist three years ago to bury the truth, not keep it. Betrayal hardens into purpose.

chapters.title: The Open Crypt
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Lured by a note in his own handwriting, Orsen descends into the crypt at night and finds Hale waiting, who confesses with serene pride: he built the town's peace on a false verdict and a curated witness. The dead clerk was his archivist-turned-blackmailer. Hale offers Orsen a clean slate — one more forgetting. Orsen refuses, and Hale moves to make the crypt hold two secrets.

chapters.title: Read Into the Record
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, climax and resolution. Elodie arrives with the recovered ledger and the town's leading citizens, forcing the confession into public record inside the very cathedral. Hale is arrested; Canon Wren's name is cleared at last. Orsen, unable to recover all he lost, chooses to build new memory rather than mourn the old — filing the truth where everyone can read it.
